document: EU GMP (EudraLex Vol 4) Annex 11 Computerised Systems
version_or_date: Revision of January 2011, in operation since 30 June 2011
notes: Still the operative text as of the latest evidence found (secondary reports dated Jul-Aug 2026 say EudraLex still lists the 2011 version). Official PDF: https://health.ec.europa.eu/system/files/2016-11/annex11_01-2011_en_0.pdf. Note: the EU and PIC/S primary sites were unreachable from this research environment (egress blocked), so clause content was cross-checked through web-search excerpts rather than a direct read of the PDF.

requirement: Moving a GMP activity from paper/manual handling onto a computerised system must not lower product quality, weaken process control or dilute quality assurance, and must not raise the overall process risk. The application software has to be validated and the IT infrastructure it runs on has to be qualified.
system_implications: Every control that exists in the paper BMR (line clearance sign-off, second-person checks, yield reconciliation, label reconciliation, in-process checks) needs an equal or stronger electronic control in the eBMR. The vendor/customer must be able to deliver validation evidence for the configured application (recipes, workflows, calculations, interfaces) and qualification evidence for servers, database, network and any cloud tenancy.
verification_test: Inspect a paper-to-electronic control mapping matrix: each paper control maps to a named system control and at least one executed test case. Confirm approved infrastructure qualification records and application validation summary report exist for the release under test.

requirement: Risk management must be applied across the whole system lifecycle, weighing patient safety, data integrity and product quality; how far validation and data-integrity controls go must be decided on a documented, justified risk basis.
system_implications: The eBMR should let the regulated user tag each data field / step with a criticality class (e.g., critical process parameter, GMP-relevant, informational) and drive controls from that tag: second-person verification, mandatory reason-for-change, audit-trail review flags, and exception reporting. The risk assessment behind the classification must be stored/linked as a controlled document. Injectables will typically classify more steps as critical (aseptic interventions, sterilisation, filtration, environmental monitoring excursions) than tablets.
verification_test: Pick a sample of recipe steps; confirm each has a criticality classification traceable to an approved risk assessment and that the behaviour (e.g., witness required) changes when the classification changes, under change control.

requirement: The company must keep a current inventory of its GMP-relevant systems and what GMP functions they perform; for critical systems it must also maintain an up-to-date description covering physical and logical layout, data flows, interfaces to other systems or processes, hardware/software prerequisites and security measures.
system_implications: The eBMR vendor must supply (and keep current per release) an architecture/system description: modules, database, integration points (ERP/material management, LIMS, weighing scales, SCADA/PLC, historian, label printers, QMS for deviations), data flow diagrams, and security design. The system should be able to export its own configuration inventory (interfaces enabled, versions) to help keep the description current.
verification_test: Compare the documented interface list with the interfaces actually configured in the production instance; any undocumented interface is a failure. Confirm the description is version-controlled and was updated at the last change.

requirement: When data move to another format or another system, validation must show that neither the values nor the meaning of the data changed during the migration.
system_implications: Upgrades, database migrations, archive exports and legacy-record imports must include automated reconciliation: record counts, checksums/hashes per record, field-level comparison of values and units, and preservation of audit trail, signatures and metadata. Signature manifestations and audit-trail links must survive migration and remain bound to the same records.
verification_test: Run a migration on a validation copy; compare source vs target record counts and hashes; spot-check that audit trails, e-signature meaning/date/time, units and precision are unchanged; confirm the migration report is approved before go-live.

requirement: Where critical data are keyed in by hand, a further accuracy check is needed, done either by a second person or by an electronic means that has itself been validated; how critical a value is, and what a wrong entry could cause, must be judged through risk management.
system_implications: For fields classified critical (e.g., dispensed weight typed manually, lot number of an API, compression force set-point, fill volume/weight, sterilisation cycle parameters, filter integrity test result), the eBMR must either (a) capture the value directly from the instrument/scale/PLC or verify it by barcode scan against the expected item, or (b) force an independent second-user verification with its own authentication before the step can be completed. The verifier must be a different user from the performer (system-enforced), and both identities, timestamps and the verified value are stored.
verification_test: Configure a critical manual field; attempt to complete the step without verification (must block); attempt verification by the same user (must be rejected); verify by a second user and check the audit record holds both identities and times. Test that a barcode mismatch blocks progression.

requirement: Stored data must be protected against damage by both physical and electronic measures, must be checked to stay accessible, readable and accurate, and must remain accessible for the entire retention period.
system_implications: Database and file storage must sit on protected, redundant infrastructure; the system should provide integrity checking (e.g., record-level hashes or database consistency checks) and a retrievability check that proves old batch records can still be opened and rendered with their audit trail and signatures. Retention rules per record type (EU batch documentation: at least one year beyond expiry or five years after QP certification, whichever is longer, per EU GMP Chapter 4) must be configurable and must block premature deletion.
verification_test: Restore/open a batch record older than the current software version and confirm full rendering incl. audit trail and signatures; attempt to delete a record inside its retention period (must be blocked); review the output of the periodic integrity/readability check.

requirement: All relevant data must be backed up regularly; the integrity and accuracy of backups and the ability to restore them must be proven during validation and then monitored periodically.
system_implications: Backups must cover the database, attachments, configuration (recipes/master batch records, user/role definitions) and audit trails as a consistent set. Restore procedures must be documented and exercised; the system should log backup job success/failure and alert on failure. Point-in-time recovery objectives should be set by risk (an injectable line running continuous aseptic filling needs a tight recovery point so in-progress batch data are not lost).
verification_test: Perform a restore of a production backup into an isolated environment; compare record counts/hashes and open a sample of batch records with audit trails; confirm backup failure raises an alert; confirm restore test records exist at the defined frequency.

requirement: It must be possible to produce clear paper copies of electronically held data; for records that support batch release, the printout must be able to show whether any data were altered after they were first entered.
system_implications: The eBMR needs a controlled print/export of the executed batch record (human-readable, complete, paginated, with unique record ID, version and 'page x of y') in which every value that was modified after first entry is visibly flagged, ideally with original value, new value, who, when and why, or a cross-reference to the audit trail entry. The rendered copy must also show signatures with name, date/time and meaning.
verification_test: Enter a value, correct it with a reason, then generate the batch release printout/PDF: the corrected field must be flagged and the original value and change details must be visible or referenced. Confirm unchanged fields are not flagged and that the print is complete (no truncated fields).

requirement: Systems that swap data electronically with other systems need suitable built-in checks so that data are entered and processed correctly and securely, keeping the risk of corruption or loss low.
system_implications: Every interface (ERP/material status, LIMS results, balances, PLC/SCADA, historian, label printing, QMS deviations) must validate what it receives: message schema and completeness, identity matching (material code, lot, batch ID), unit and range checks, duplicate/sequence detection, acknowledgement and retry, and authenticated/encrypted transport. Failed or rejected transfers must raise a visible alert and must never silently drop or default a value into the batch record.
verification_test: Inject malformed, out-of-range, duplicate and wrong-batch messages at each interface; confirm rejection, alerting and logging. Interrupt the connection mid-transfer and confirm no partial or duplicated values land in the batch record.

requirement: Based on risk, the system should itself generate a record of every GMP-relevant change and deletion (an audit trail); the reason for changing or deleting GMP-relevant data must be captured; audit trails must be retrievable, convertible into a form people can understand, and reviewed on a regular basis.
system_implications: Every create/modify/delete of GMP data in the eBMR (step results, parameters, material entries, comments, status changes, signatures, voids) must write an append-only, system-generated entry holding user ID and full name, date/time with time zone, record/field identity, old value, new value and a mandatory reason (reason list plus free text). Ordinary users and administrators must not be able to edit, delete or switch off the trail; the trail must be viewable and exportable in plain language (not only raw database codes), filterable by batch, and flagged for review.
verification_test: Change and delete sample GMP values with each role; confirm entries appear with old/new value, reason, user and timestamp; confirm the save is blocked without a reason; attempt to edit/delete audit entries and to disable auditing via UI, API and admin console (all must fail or, for privileged DB access, be detectable via integrity hashes).

requirement: Any change to the computerised system, including changes to its configuration, may only be made in a controlled way following a defined procedure.
system_implications: Master batch records/recipes, workflows, calculations, limits, role definitions and interface settings must be version-controlled objects with draft-review-approve-effective states, e-signed approvals, and an audit trail of configuration changes. Only one effective version of a master record may be usable for new batches; in-flight batches must stay bound to the version they started on unless an approved change says otherwise. Software releases must go through a test environment before production.
verification_test: Edit a master recipe: confirm it cannot be used in production until approved; confirm running batches keep their original version; confirm configuration audit trail shows who changed what; confirm production configuration cannot be changed directly without the controlled path.

requirement: Systems must be re-assessed at intervals to confirm they are still validated and GMP-compliant; where relevant the review looks at current functionality, deviations, incidents and problems, upgrade history, performance, reliability, security and the validation status.
system_implications: The eBMR should make periodic review easy by providing reports for the review period: configuration and software changes, incident/error logs, interface failures, user-access changes and privileged activity, backup/restore results, performance/uptime, open validation gaps. These reports must be generated by the system (not hand-assembled) to be trustworthy.
verification_test: Generate the periodic-review report pack for a defined period and cross-check a sample of entries against the underlying logs; confirm the pack covers all listed topics.

requirement: Access must be limited to authorised people by physical and/or logical means (e.g., personal credentials, biometrics, access cards, locked server/storage areas); how strong these controls are should reflect how critical the system is; granting, modifying and withdrawing access rights must be recorded.
system_implications: Individual named accounts with role-based permissions (operator, verifier/witness, supervisor, QA reviewer, QP, master-data author, administrator); user administration workflow that logs every grant/change/revocation with requester, approver, date and reason; history of who held which role on any past date must be queryable. Shop-floor terminals in cleanrooms (injectables, Grade A/B gowned operators) need an authentication method usable with gloves (badge/RFID + PIN or biometrics) without resorting to shared logins.
verification_test: Create, modify and disable a user; confirm each action is logged with approver; query role membership as of a past date; confirm a disabled user cannot log in or sign; confirm there is no generic/shared account with write access.

requirement: Data and document management systems must be built so that the identity of whoever enters, changes, confirms or deletes data is recorded together with the date and time.
system_implications: Each recorded value and each confirmation (e.g., 'performed', 'verified', 'checked') must carry the authenticated user identity and a trusted server timestamp (not a client-device clock the operator can change). Timestamps should be synchronised to a reliable time source and stored with time-zone information so multi-site data line up.
verification_test: Change a terminal clock and record a step: the stored timestamp must still come from the synchronised server source. Confirm every entry, verification and deletion in a test batch shows user identity and date/time.

requirement: All incidents, not just outright system failures or data errors, must be reported and assessed; for critical incidents the root cause must be found and used as the basis for corrective and preventive action.
system_implications: The eBMR must log technical and functional incidents (interface failures, lost connections, crashes during a step, failed signatures, time-sync failures, printing failures) in a way that links them to affected batches, so an incident can be raised in the QMS and its batch impact assessed before release. Batches touched by an open incident should be flagged on the release/QP view.
verification_test: Simulate an interface outage during a weighing step; confirm an incident/event record is created, linked to the batch, and shown as open on the batch review/QP screen until closed.

requirement: Electronic records may be signed electronically. Such signatures must carry, inside the company, the same weight as a handwritten one; they must stay permanently tied to the record they sign; and they must show when (date and time) they were applied.
system_implications: Signing must require the signer's own credentials at the moment of signing; the signature object (user ID, printed full name, date/time with zone, meaning such as performed/verified/reviewed/approved/certified) must be stored bound to the exact record version (e.g., via record hash), must display on screen and on every rendered copy, and cannot be copied, moved or re-used on another record. A company policy/attestation that users accept e-signatures as equivalent to handwritten ones should be captured in the system (acknowledgement at account activation).
verification_test: Sign a step, then inspect storage: signature references the record version/hash; try to transplant a signature to another record via API/DB manipulation (must be rejected or detected); confirm signature manifestation appears on screen and on the printout with name, date/time and meaning.

requirement: If the computerised system records certification and batch release, it must permit only Qualified Persons to certify release, must clearly identify and record who released or certified each batch, and this act must be done with an electronic signature.
system_implications: A distinct 'QP certification' permission, granted only to persons named as QP on the manufacturing/import authorisation (with an approval workflow and a register of QP accounts). Certification is an e-signature with the meaning 'certified by QP' and the QP's identity; release status changes (quarantine to certified/released) must be possible only through this action and must feed downstream systems (ERP/warehouse) to lift quarantine. Other users, including admins and QA reviewers without QP status, must not be able to certify.
verification_test: Attempt certification with QA reviewer, supervisor and admin accounts (must fail); certify with a QP account and confirm the record shows QP name, date/time, meaning; confirm ERP stock status changes only after certification.

requirement: For systems that support critical processes, arrangements must exist to keep those processes going if the system breaks down (for example a manual or alternative system); how fast the fallback must be in place is set by risk and by the process it supports; the arrangements must be documented and tested.
system_implications: Provide a validated downtime mode: controlled pre-printed/printable emergency batch record sheets generated from the current master record (uniquely numbered, reconciled), local buffering on the shop floor for short network outages with guaranteed ordered re-sync, and a controlled back-entry procedure after recovery where late-entered data are flagged as transcribed from paper, second-person verified, and linked to the scanned original. Injectables: an aseptic filling run cannot simply stop, so fallback must be immediate and pre-staged; tablets may tolerate a planned pause at defined hold points.
verification_test: Execute a downtime drill: cut the network mid-batch, continue on the fallback, restore, back-enter data; confirm back-entered values are flagged, verified, linked to scanned originals and time-stamped with both the original execution time and the entry time.

requirement: Data may be moved to an archive; archived data must be checked for accessibility, readability and integrity, and before relevant changes to the system (hardware or software) the ability to retrieve archived data must be confirmed and tested.
system_implications: Archive function that moves completed, released batch records (with full audit trail, signatures, attachments and metadata) into read-only storage, with fixity checks (hashes) run periodically and a restore/re-render capability that still works after application upgrades. Upgrade validation must include retrieval tests of archived records from earlier versions.
verification_test: Archive a batch, run fixity check, then upgrade the application in a test environment and retrieve/render the archived record; confirm content, audit trail and signatures are intact and hashes match.

requirement: Process owner, system owner, QPs and IT must work closely together and everyone must have suitable qualifications, access level and defined responsibilities. When third parties supply or run the system (including hosting/service providers), formal written agreements must set out responsibilities; supplier competence and reliability are key selection factors and the need for a supplier audit is set by risk; the supplier's quality information and audit findings must be available to inspectors on request.
system_implications: Roles for process owner and system owner should be configurable in the system and shown on validation/periodic review outputs. For a SaaS or vendor-hosted eBMR: a quality/technical agreement covering data ownership, backup, change notification, incident reporting, audit-trail retention, access for inspections and exit/data return; the vendor should support customer audits and provide release notes and validation packages.
verification_test: Check the quality agreement covers the listed topics; confirm the vendor audit report is on file with a risk-based rationale; confirm the system shows named process and system owners.

requirement: User requirements must describe the needed functions, be grounded in documented risk assessment and GMP impact, and be traceable across the lifecycle. Validation must show suitable test methods and scenarios, paying particular attention to process parameter limits, data limits and error handling; automated test tools and test environments need a documented assessment of their adequacy.
system_implications: Maintain a URS-to-test traceability matrix per configured product/recipe. The eBMR must enforce configured limits (warning vs action/reject limits for weights, in-process results, CPPs) and must handle errors deterministically (e.g., instrument disconnect, invalid barcode, double submission) - all of which must be tested, including boundary values. If automated/regression testing tools are used, keep an assessment of their fitness.
verification_test: Boundary tests on each critical limit (just inside, on, just outside); negative tests for error paths; review traceability matrix completeness; confirm the test-tool assessment exists.

document: EU GMP / PIC/S Annex 11 Computerised Systems - draft revision (with revised Chapter 4 and new Annex 22)
version_or_date: Draft published 7 July 2025 for stakeholder consultation; consultation closed 7 October 2025
status: draft - NOT finalised as of the latest evidence found (secondary reports dated July-August 2026 say EudraLex still shows the 2011 Annex 11; final text originally expected mid-2026, operative date not announced; some commentators estimate implementation not before 2027)
notes: Drafted jointly by the EMA GMDP Inspectors Working Group and PIC/S. Grows from about 5 to about 19 pages in 17 sections (scope; principles; pharmaceutical quality system; risk management; personnel and training; requirements; supplier and service management; alarms; qualification and validation; handling of data; identity and access management; audit trails; electronic signatures; periodic review; security; backup; archiving) plus glossary. Section numbers for sections 7, 8, 10-15 were confirmed via secondary sources; the remaining numbering is inferred. Consultation page: https://health.ec.europa.eu/consultations/stakeholders-consultation-eudralex-volume-4-good-manufacturing-practice-guidelines-chapter-4-annex_en . Design recommendation: build the eBMR to the draft now, since it is stricter and largely codifies current inspector expectations, but cite the 2011 text as the binding reference until the final version is published.

requirement: The draft widens and hardens the audit trail rule: wherever users can create, modify or delete GMP data, the system must automatically log each such manual interaction, now including the creation of data and not only changes/deletions. Each entry should identify who acted (with role), what changed (previous and new value), when (with time zone where relevant) and why (the system should prompt for the reason). The audit trail is to be configured and switched on from installation and should not be possible to turn off, edit or delete; commentators note the draft still tolerates such functions being reachable only by administrators independent of GMP work.
system_implications: No configuration switch that disables auditing of GMP data in production; the audit log is append-only and tamper-evident (e.g., hash chaining); entries include creation events; each entry holds user ID, full name, role at the time, old value, new value, UTC timestamp plus local zone, and a prompted reason (controlled list plus free text). Any privileged maintenance that could affect audit data must itself be logged and restricted to admins with no GMP role. Keep data audit trails distinct from technical/system event logs so reviewers see GMP-relevant entries clearly.
verification_test: Create, modify and delete values as operator/supervisor/QA: confirm entries for all three event types with role, old/new, zone-aware time and reason; search the admin console and API for any disable/purge function; attempt direct DB edit and confirm tamper detection flags the chain break.

requirement: Per secondary analyses of the draft: audit trail review must be governed by a written procedure, performed by someone independent of the business process being reviewed, documented, and may be done as part of batch record review; discrepancies found must be investigated, resolved and escalated per a defined route; review frequency is risk-based, and QPs must be given access to the relevant audit trail entries.
system_implications: Build audit-trail review into the batch review workflow: a batch-scoped audit trail view that highlights GMP-critical changes (value changes after first entry, deletions, voids, late entries, re-opened steps, signature failures) with a 'reviewed' e-signature by a reviewer who did not execute the batch (system-enforced), a way to raise/link a deviation from any entry, and blocking of batch disposition while review is incomplete or discrepancies are open. Grant QP role read access to the complete audit trail. Provide validated exception reports so review focuses on meaningful events rather than every log line.
verification_test: Execute a batch with changes; attempt batch review sign-off by a user who executed steps (must be blocked); confirm the exception report lists all post-entry changes; confirm open discrepancy blocks disposition; confirm QP account can open the full audit trail for the batch.

requirement: According to published analyses, the draft no longer carries a stand-alone clause on QP batch certification by electronic signature (that topic is left to Annex 16); instead it requires that QPs can access audit trail entries. Until the draft is final, the 2011 clause 15 still applies.
system_implications: Keep the QP-only e-signature certification (A11-17) - it remains required today and remains good practice under Annex 16 - and additionally ensure the QP certification screen gives one-click access to the batch audit trail and review outcome. Do not design on the assumption that the QP e-signature control can be dropped.
verification_test: Confirm QP-only certification still enforced (see A11-17) and that the QP certification screen links to the full batch audit trail and audit-trail review record.

requirement: Per secondary analyses, the draft expects: the signer to re-authenticate when signing; the meaning of the signature (e.g., review, approval) to be clear to the signer at the time of signing; the displayed/printed signature to show the signer's name, role, meaning, and date/time with time zone where applicable; and, for hybrid set-ups where a handwritten signature relates to an electronic record, measures that give high confidence that any later change to the electronic record invalidates the signature. It also references use of external (trust service) e-signature providers.
system_implications: At signing: fresh credential entry (password/PIN, biometric or badge+PIN) even within an active session; the dialog states the meaning explicitly ('I verify the dispensed quantity of lot X'). Store meaning, role, UTC time and zone. Bind the signature to a hash of the signed content; if the content changes after signing, the system must automatically mark the signature invalid/superseded and require re-signing, and show the record as unsigned in the meantime. Avoid hybrid wet-ink signing on printouts of eBMR data; if unavoidable, link scanned signed pages to the electronic record version hash.
verification_test: Sign a record, then change a value: the prior signature must show as invalidated and the step must require re-signature. Confirm the signing dialog requires credential re-entry and shows meaning; inspect manifestation for name, role, meaning, date/time and zone on screen and PDF.

clause: 12 (Audit trails - timing of review relative to release)
requirement: Secondary summaries of the draft report that review of audit trails should be targeted and risk-based (not line-by-line), done by persons not involved in the reviewed activity, and completed before batch release unless a later review is justified; audit-trail review outcomes that bear directly on product release should be available to the QP when certifying.
system_implications: Batch disposition/QP certification must be blocked until the batch-scoped audit trail review is signed off (or a documented, approved justification for deferral exists). The QP certification screen must display the audit-trail review status, reviewer, date, findings and any linked deviations. Review scope rules (which event types, which data classes) should be configurable per product/process risk and version-controlled.
verification_test: Try to certify a batch with no audit-trail review record (must be blocked); record a justified deferral and confirm it requires QA approval and appears on the QP view; confirm reviewer independence is enforced.

requirement: The draft replaces the short 2011 security clause with a detailed identity and access management section. Reported expectations: unique personal accounts (shared accounts tolerated only for read-only use, never for creating or changing data); least privilege (no more rights than the job needs); segregation of duties so that people doing GMP work do not also hold administrator privileges; multi-factor authentication for remote access to critical systems; automatic lock-out after repeated failed log-ins; and controlled, timely handling and review of access rights.
system_implications: Enforce one identity per person (SSO/IdP integration allowed), no shared write-capable accounts, role catalogue with least-privilege defaults, hard separation between GMP roles and system-administration roles (system prevents a user holding both), MFA for any remote or vendor access, lock after a configurable number of failed attempts, idle-session lock on shop-floor clients, prompt deprovisioning on leaver events from HR/IdP, and a periodic access-recertification report listing each user, role, last login and approver.
verification_test: Try assigning an administrator role to a user holding operator/QA/QP roles (must be refused); exceed the failed-login threshold (account locks, event logged); connect remotely without second factor (refused); run access recertification report and confirm it lists all accounts with roles and last activity.

requirement: Alarms were not covered in 2011; the draft adds a dedicated section. Reported expectations: GMP-relevant alarms and their acknowledgements are logged automatically with full details; alarm handling and verification are documented (for example in the batch record) with a log that cannot be erased or deactivated; alarm logs are reviewed periodically for handling and trends. Alarm/event logs are distinct from the audit trail of manual data changes.
system_implications: The eBMR (or the connected SCADA/EMS feeding it) must bring GMP alarms occurring during a batch (e.g., out-of-limit temperature/humidity, pressure cascade loss, particle count excursions, compression force out of range, checkweigher rejects, sterilisation/depyrogenation cycle faults) into the batch context: time raised, time acknowledged, who acknowledged, comment/action, and link to deviation where required. Alarm limits are controlled configuration. Provide an alarm log per batch and trending across batches. Injectables: aseptic-area alarms (differential pressure, particle monitoring, isolator/RABS glove breach, filter integrity failures) will dominate and must be visible to reviewers and the QP.
verification_test: Generate a simulated out-of-limit event during a batch: confirm it appears in the batch alarm log with raise/ack times, acknowledger identity and comment; confirm acknowledgement without comment is prevented for GMP-critical alarms; confirm the log cannot be deleted; run the alarm trend report.

requirement: Reported to cover four themes: verification of input (plausibility checks for manually entered critical data, plus second-person or validated electronic verification); data transfer (preference for validated electronic interfaces over manual transcription, with manual transfer treated as an exception needing extra control); controlled and validated data migration; and risk-based encryption of critical data in storage and in transit.
system_implications: Field-level plausibility rules (type, range, format, expected lot/material match, unit consistency); direct capture from balances, PLCs, checkweighers, LIMS and environmental monitoring instead of manual typing wherever feasible; when manual transcription is unavoidable, force double verification and mark the value as manually transcribed; encryption at rest (database, backups, archives) and in transit (TLS for all clients and interfaces); validated migration tooling with reconciliation reports.
verification_test: Enter implausible values (wrong unit, out-of-range, wrong lot) and confirm rejection/warning; confirm interface-captured values are marked as such and cannot be overwritten without audit; confirm manually transcribed values require verification; confirm TLS on all endpoints and encryption of database files/backups.

requirement: Cyber/IT security becomes an explicit GMP expectation. Reported content: firewalls and network segmentation, timely patching, protection against malware, restrictions on removable media, disaster recovery with defined recovery time and recovery point objectives, isolation of unsupported/unpatched platforms, multi-factor authentication for remote access to critical systems, and (reported as draft 15.19) regular penetration testing of critical systems that are exposed to the internet.
system_implications: Vendor and customer must evidence a security baseline for the eBMR stack: supported OS/DB versions with patch SLAs, hardened shop-floor clients (kiosk mode, USB storage disabled), network zoning between OT (line PLCs) and IT, malware protection on servers/clients, documented RTO/RPO per module (a stricter RPO for the execution module during aseptic filling than for reporting), DR runbooks tested, and periodic penetration tests for internet-facing/SaaS deployments with remediation tracking.
verification_test: Review last penetration test report and remediation closure; attempt to mount USB storage on a shop-floor client (blocked); check patch levels against vendor support matrix; run a DR exercise and compare achieved recovery time/point to targets.

requirement: The draft expands both topics: backups must be kept physically and logically separate from the primary data and restore capability must be tested regularly; archiving receives its own, more detailed section than in 2011 (retention, protection and retrievability of archived records).
system_implications: Backups written to a separate site/account (immutable or write-once storage preferred so ransomware or an admin cannot alter them), encrypted, with scheduled restore tests whose results are recorded; archives read-only with fixity checks and retrieval tests across software versions (see A11-07, A11-19).
verification_test: Confirm backup target is on separate infrastructure/credentials; attempt deletion of a backup with production admin credentials (should fail if immutable); review restore-test log for the defined frequency; retrieve an archived record.

requirement: Periodic review grows from one sentence in 2011 to a section of about twelve sub-clauses. Secondary summaries mention review of system documentation, maintenance, service agreements, adequacy of backup, disaster recovery and archiving arrangements, data integrity status, changes in regulatory requirements, training effectiveness, and ongoing confirmation of validated status (a one-off qualification is not enough).
system_implications: Provide a periodic review dashboard/report pack generated from system data for a chosen period: changes and releases, open validation gaps, incidents and interface failures, user and privileged-access changes, audit-trail review completion rates, backup/restore and DR test results, supplier SLA performance, alarm statistics, training status of active users. Store the approved periodic review report and its actions in or linked to the system.
verification_test: Generate the pack for a test period and trace a sample of each metric to underlying records; confirm the pack covers each topic listed in the site's periodic review SOP mapped to draft section 14.

requirement: The regulated company stays fully responsible for GMP compliance even when a vendor, cloud/SaaS provider or internal IT runs the system. Suppliers and service providers must be qualified (audit as needed) and covered by written agreements/contracts that fix responsibilities, including data ownership and access, security, communication of security issues, support during inspections, and an exit strategy; complete validation documentation must be accessible for cloud services.
system_implications: For a SaaS eBMR: contractual right to audit, inspection support, notification of security incidents and planned changes, data residency and ownership, return/export of all records with audit trails and signatures in a readable format on exit, and access to the provider's qualification and validation evidence. The product should support a full, validated export of the customer's data set to make the exit clause workable.
verification_test: Review the contract/quality agreement against the listed elements; perform a trial full export of a test tenant and re-open batch records with audit trails and signatures in the export viewer.

document: EU GMP / PIC/S Annex 22 Artificial Intelligence (new)
version_or_date: Draft published 7 July 2025; consultation closed 7 October 2025; EMA multistakeholder expert workshop held 30 June - 1 July 2026
status: draft - not finalised as of the latest evidence found (secondary reports dated August 2026: no final Annex 22 in EudraLex; PIC/S still lists it under drafts)
notes: Draft scope: static AI/ML models with deterministic output (same input gives same output) used in critical GMP applications; dynamic/continuously learning, probabilistic-output, generative AI and LLMs excluded from critical GMP use, allowed only in non-critical uses under human-in-the-loop oversight. After consultation, the drafting group is reported to be considering whether and under what safeguards dynamic/generative models might be addressed - scope may change in the final text.

requirement: If AI/ML is used in a critical GMP function, the draft limits it to static, deterministic models and expects a precisely defined intended use, predefined performance/acceptance metrics, representative test data kept independent of training data, explainability and confidence information for outputs, change control, and ongoing performance monitoring; generative AI/LLMs only for non-critical tasks with a human in the loop.
system_implications: Keep AI out of GMP decision paths in the eBMR (e.g., no AI auto-approval of steps, deviations or release) unless the model is static, validated and governed as above. Any AI helper (e.g., drafting deviation text, summarising a batch for the reviewer, visual inspection of tablets or vials) must be flagged as such, its output must be reviewed and signed by a human, and the model version and confidence must be recorded with the output. Injectables: AI-based automated visual inspection of filled units would be a critical application needing full Annex 22-style validation.
verification_test: Inventory all AI/ML features; confirm none can change GMP data or status without human e-signature; for any critical-use model, confirm locked version, documented test set independence, acceptance metrics and monitoring records.

document: EU GMP Chapter 4 Documentation - draft revision
version_or_date: Draft published 7 July 2025 with Annex 11/22; consultation closed 7 October 2025
status: draft - not finalised as of latest evidence found; current binding text is the Chapter 4 revision in force since 30 June 2011
notes: Draft introduces a data governance system integrated into the PQS, a data lifecycle model (reported as section 4.12), codified ALCOA++ definitions (adding Traceable), explicit hybrid-system controls (reported as sections 4.82-4.85) and explicit recognition of electronic signatures. Consultation document: https://health.ec.europa.eu/document/download/fa336a6e-753b-46fc-b53b-9178bacd8878_en?filename=mp_vol4_chap4_consultation_guideline_en.pdf

source: EU GMP Chapter 4 Documentation (2011, in force)
requirement: Documents and records can be partly electronic and partly paper; for both mixed and single-format systems the company must state how master documents, official copies, data handling and records relate to each other and how each is controlled.
system_implications: The eBMR configuration must define which object is the master (the approved electronic master batch record/recipe), which outputs are official copies (controlled PDFs/prints, watermarked 'copy' with generation date and version), and which is the original record of execution (the electronic record with its audit trail). Any remaining paper elements (e.g., printed labels, instrument printouts, EM plates) need a defined link to the electronic batch (scan + reconciliation + reference ID).
verification_test: Review the documented record map; print a copy and confirm it is marked as an uncontrolled/official copy with version and date; confirm each paper artefact type has a defined linkage and reconciliation check in the eBMR.

source: EU GMP Chapter 4 Documentation (2011, in force)
requirement: Batch documentation has to be kept for one year beyond the expiry date of the batch or for at least five years after QP certification, whichever period ends later.
system_implications: Retention end date must be computed per batch as the later of (expiry + 1 year) and (QP certification date + 5 years), be longer if other markets or company policy require it, and block purge/archiving-with-deletion before that date. Audit trails, signatures and metadata inherit the same retention as the batch record.
verification_test: For test batches with different expiry and certification dates, verify the computed retention date; attempt deletion before the date (blocked, logged).

source: EU GMP Chapter 4 Documentation - draft revision (July 2025)
clause: Data governance and data lifecycle (reported as 4.12 onward)
requirement: The draft requires a data governance system, integrated in the PQS and applying whatever the format (paper, electronic, hybrid), covering the whole data lifecycle - reported as creation, processing, verification, decision-making, retention and controlled destruction - and treating metadata and audit trails as part of the record, with defined ownership.
system_implications: Model each eBMR data element with its lifecycle state (captured, verified, reviewed, used for decision/released, archived, eligible for destruction) and keep metadata (units, instrument ID, method/recipe version, user, time, context) inseparable from the value. Destruction at end of retention must be an authorised, recorded act.
verification_test: Trace one critical value from capture through verification, review, QP decision and archive, confirming metadata and audit trail travel with it; confirm destruction requires authorisation and leaves a destruction record.

source: EU GMP Chapter 4 Documentation - draft revision (July 2025)
requirement: Per secondary summaries, the draft gives hybrid (paper plus electronic) systems specific attention: they must be clearly defined, validated and risk-controlled, with procedures for the hand-offs between manual and computerised parts; the draft also expressly recognises electronic signatures in GMP documentation.
system_implications: Minimise hybrid steps in the eBMR; where they remain (downtime sheets, external lab certificates, instrument printouts), the system must record the linkage (scan, unique ID, who attached, when), verify completeness (all issued sheets returned) and prevent the paper and electronic versions from diverging. Electronic signatures should be the default signing method everywhere in the batch record.
verification_test: Run a hybrid scenario (downtime sheet); confirm issuance log, return reconciliation, scan attachment with audit trail and second-person verification of transcribed values.

document: EMA GMP/GDP Questions and Answers - Data integrity section (EMA GMDP Inspectors Working Group)
version_or_date: Published August 2016 (23 Q&As); no replacement found
status: final (current EU interpretive guidance; complements Annex 11 and Chapter 4)
notes: Hosted on the EMA GMP Q&A page: https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/human-regulatory-overview/research-development/compliance-research-development/good-manufacturing-practice/guidance-good-manufacturing-practice-good-distribution-practice-questions-answers . EMA site was unreachable from this environment; content checked through web-search excerpts of copies of the Q&A. Where the 2025 Annex 11/Chapter 4 drafts become final they are expected to absorb much of this Q&A.

source: EMA GMP Q&A on data integrity (Aug 2016)
clause: Q&A on assessing data risk / data lifecycle
requirement: Data risk should be judged by how exposed the data are to accidental or intentional amendment, deletion or re-creation; controls that stop unauthorised actions or make them more visible/detectable reduce risk. The assessment should focus on the business process (production, QC) and factors such as complexity, consistency, degree of automation vs human input, and subjectivity of outcomes, at every lifecycle stage. Holding data in temporary memory before it is saved is flagged as a risk because changes there are often not audit-trailed; removing or shortening such temporary storage lowers the risk.
system_implications: Commit every GMP entry to durable, audit-trailed storage at the moment the user confirms it (no editable client-side drafts of executed steps, no end-of-shift bulk save, no 'offline edit then sync' without audit trail of each local action). Where short offline buffering is unavoidable, the buffered entries must be signed/time-stamped at capture and made immutable before sync. Prefer automated capture over subjective manual entry for critical values.
verification_test: Enter a value, kill the client before 'save' and confirm no unsaved-but-editable GMP value can later be silently submitted; inspect the offline buffer (if any) for immutability and capture timestamps; confirm each step completion creates its audit record immediately.

source: EMA GMP Q&A on data integrity (Aug 2016)
clause: Q&A on review of electronic data / review by exception
requirement: Quality risk management may be applied to reviewing electronic data, and review by exception is acceptable when scientifically justified; exception reports are named as a common way to focus review of electronic batch records, and how much of the full eBR is reviewed can depend on the exceptions and on experience with the process. The automated system and its batch exception report must be properly tested and validated. Reviewing printouts alone risks missing data (e.g., un-investigated OOS or anomalies); reviewing the electronic raw data helps detect deletion, amendment, duplication, re-use and fabrication.
system_implications: Provide a validated 'review by exception' report per batch listing every out-of-limit value, alarm, deviation, manual override, value changed after first entry, re-performed step, late or back-dated entry, skipped/NA step, signature failure and audit-trail anomaly, with drill-down to the full record. Reviewers must work in the system on the electronic record (not only on PDFs). Exception rules are controlled configuration; the report's completeness must be proven in validation (seeded-exception testing).
verification_test: Seed a test batch with one instance of each exception type and confirm the exception report lists all of them (no false negatives); change an exception rule and confirm it requires change control; confirm the reviewer signs the review within the system.

source: EMA GMP Q&A on data integrity (Aug 2016)
clause: Q&A on control of blank/template forms
requirement: Paper templates for GMP records must be handed out in a controlled, traceable way so that a record cannot be quietly re-created: the site should be able to show who received how many uniquely identified copies, when and for which area, and the copies should be made hard to duplicate without detection.
system_implications: Applies to any paper the eBMR still issues - downtime/contingency batch sheets, label reconciliation sheets, EM sampling sheets: the system should print them only through a controlled issuance function that assigns unique serial numbers, records issuer/date/quantity/destination, marks each page (batch ID, serial, page x/y, issue stamp) and later forces reconciliation of every issued page (returned, used, voided) before batch closure.
verification_test: Issue three contingency sheets, return two, and attempt to close the batch (must be blocked until the third is reconciled as used/voided); try printing an uncontrolled copy of a template (not possible from user roles).

source: EMA GMP Q&A on data integrity (Aug 2016)
clause: Q&A on outsourced activities / chain of contracts
requirement: Through the chain of contracts it must be ensured that the integrity of records about manufacturing activities is secured throughout their retention period at a site holding a manufacturing/import authorisation; a recipient of supplier documents (e.g., certificates of analysis) should understand the supplier's systems and procedures for producing them and be told of significant changes.
system_implications: When the eBMR is operated by a CMO or hosted by a SaaS vendor, the MIA holder must retain contractual and technical access to complete batch records (with audit trails and signatures) for the full retention period, including after contract end. Supplier CoA data imported into the eBMR should record their source and be subject to supplier-qualification status checks.
verification_test: Confirm contract terms for record access/retention; test that a complete batch record export can be produced for the MIA holder; confirm imported CoA data carry source metadata.

document: EU GMP Annex 16 Certification by a Qualified Person and Batch Release
version_or_date: Published 12 October 2015; in operation since 15 April 2016
status: final (current); no revision in progress found
notes: Official PDF: https://health.ec.europa.eu/document/download/20c41532-33d5-4635-ae80-8735d3d09fe0_en?filename=v4_an16_201510_en.pdf . EMA GMP Q&As on Annex 16 (unexpected deviations, registered specifications) supplement it. Content checked via web-search excerpts; primary site unreachable from this environment.

requirement: Before release, the QP must be satisfied that each individual batch was made and tested in line with applicable law, the marketing authorisation (MA) and GMP.
system_implications: Each master batch record/recipe version must carry an explicit link to the MA/registered details it implements (product, strength, pack, registered process steps/parameters, registered in-process and finished-product specifications, approved manufacturing sites) and to the variation/change control that approved it. The QP view must show, for the executed batch, which master version was used and whether it matched the MA status in force for the target market(s) at manufacture; mismatches must be flagged.
verification_test: Execute a batch on a master version later superseded by a variation; confirm the QP view shows the version and the MA-alignment status; attempt to execute a batch on a master version not linked to an approved MA/change record (must be blocked).

clause: 1.7 (matters the QP must ensure, directly or by reliance on the PQS)
requirement: The QP must be assured (personally or by well-founded, continuously verified reliance on the quality system) that, among other things: production and QC deviations and changes were authorised by the responsible people; required checks and tests were done and production/QC documentation is complete and approved; processes and test methods are validated and consistent with the MA; all batch-related investigations, including out-of-specification and out-of-trend ones, are complete enough to support certification; and the effect of any open complaints, investigations or recalls has been assessed.
system_implications: A QP certification cockpit that aggregates, per batch, live status from eBMR and linked QMS/LIMS/ERP: record completeness (no open, skipped or unsigned steps; no blank mandatory fields), all deviations and change controls with their approval/closure state, OOS/OOT investigations and their stage, in-process results vs limits, material release status, equipment/room qualification and calibration status at time of use, process validation status of the product, and open complaints/recalls/investigations for the product. Certification is blocked while mandatory checks are red, unless the QP records a justified decision that is itself captured and reviewable.
verification_test: Create a batch with an open deviation, an open OOS and an unsigned step: confirm each is shown on the cockpit and certification is blocked; close each and confirm the block lifts; confirm the cockpit data are pulled live (timestamped) not manually entered.

source: EU GMP Annex 16 (2015/2016) with EMA GMP Q&A on Annex 16
requirement: A QP may certify a batch affected by an unexpected deviation from MA and/or GMP details in the manufacturing process or analytical controls only if registered specifications are still met, the deviation has been properly investigated with its root cause corrected, and a documented quality-risk assessment supports it (with consideration of whether a variation is needed). Per the EMA Q&A, registered specifications include the in-process, bulk and finished-product specifications in the MA; failing a registered finished-product specification takes the batch outside this route; in-process deviations may be acceptable only where risk assessment shows no impact; the same deviation recurring after discovery is to be handled as a change needing a variation; and the manufacturer must keep a record of batches certified under this provision for management review and product quality review.
system_implications: In-process limits in the master record must be tagged as 'registered (MA)' vs 'internal/alert' so a failure of a registered limit auto-raises a deviation classified as MA-relevant and appears on the QP cockpit with its risk assessment. The deviation record must capture: unexpected-deviation flag, registered-spec impact, root cause, risk assessment reference, variation assessment. Keep a queryable register of batches certified with unexpected deviations for the PQR. Recurrence detection: warn when the same deviation type recurs on subsequent batches after first discovery.
verification_test: Force a registered in-process limit failure: confirm automatic deviation with MA-relevant flag, QP cockpit visibility, and inclusion in the 'certified under unexpected deviation' register after certification; repeat on a second batch and confirm the recurrence warning.

requirement: QP certifications must be entered in a register or equivalent document that is kept current as certifications happen and remains available to competent-authority inspectors for the period national law requires, and at least five years.
system_implications: The system must write each certification (batch number, product/strength/pack, market(s), certifying QP identity, date/time, reference to confirmations relied on) into an append-only QP register at the moment of e-signature, viewable and exportable for inspectors, with retention of at least five years (longer if national law or batch-record retention requires).
verification_test: Certify a batch and confirm a register entry appears immediately with all fields; attempt to edit/delete the entry (must be prevented or audit-trailed with reason); export the register for a date range.

requirement: A batch may be released to the market only after QP certification; until then it stays at the manufacturing site or moves under quarantine to an approved site. Safeguards must stop uncertified batches reaching saleable stock; they may be physical (segregation, labelling) or electronic (validated computerised systems), and must persist when uncertified stock moves between authorised sites. The way QP certification is notified to the site that transfers stock to saleable status must be set out in a technical agreement and the notification must be formal, unambiguous and follow Chapter 4 documentation rules.
system_implications: The eBMR must be the (or feed the) validated electronic quarantine interlock: batch status stays 'quarantine/uncertified' in ERP/WMS until the QP certification event arrives; shipping/allocation transactions for uncertified batches are rejected; inter-site transfers carry the quarantine status; the certification notification sent to the release/distribution site is a structured, signed, audit-trailed message (batch, product, market, QP, date/time) with acknowledgement. Any manual override of quarantine status must be impossible for ordinary roles and fully audit-trailed.
verification_test: Attempt to allocate/ship an uncertified batch in ERP/WMS (rejected); transfer it between sites (status preserved); certify and confirm the notification message is received, acknowledged and logged; attempt manual status override with non-QP roles (rejected).

clause: Partial manufacturing confirmations (section 1 and Appendix I)
requirement: Where another site performs only part of the manufacture, a QP at that site must at least confirm that its operations followed GMP and the written agreement, and the certifying QP may rely on such confirmations. Appendix I defines what the confirmation must contain; in summary it identifies the confirming site and QP, ties the statement to the governing technical/quality agreement, states the GMP compliance being confirmed, and is signed and dated.
system_implications: Support recording and linking of upstream confirmations (e.g., bulk tablets from a contract site, or a sterile bulk/filled unlabelled vials from a CMO) to the finished batch: structured fields matching Appendix I, attached signed document or electronic signature from the partner, and a check that every upstream stage in the batch genealogy has a confirmation before final certification.
verification_test: Build a batch genealogy with one external bulk stage lacking confirmation: certification blocked; add a confirmation with all Appendix I fields: block lifts; confirmation visible in the QP register entry.

requirement: Reported to contain about six clauses on documenting user requirements and the application configuration, making a traceability matrix mandatory and allowing modern electronic tools to be used to author and maintain requirements; requirements are to be kept current across the lifecycle.
system_implications: The vendor should ship a configurable-requirements baseline and a documented configuration specification per customer deployment (roles, workflows, recipes, limits, interfaces, reports). The system should export its effective configuration in a reviewable form and support linking configuration items to requirement IDs so the traceability matrix (requirement -> configuration -> test) can be generated rather than hand-maintained.
verification_test: Export effective configuration and compare with the approved configuration specification; generate the traceability matrix and confirm every requirement has at least one passing test and every configured GMP function has a requirement.

clause: 9 (Qualification and validation) and scope for cloud/service models
requirement: Per commentators, the qualification/validation section largely carries over the 2011 expectations, while the draft as a whole extends explicitly to cloud and service-based systems and expects complete validation documentation to be accessible for cloud services; critics note it lacks an explicit formal system-release step.
system_implications: Treat go-live of each eBMR release as a formally approved release decision (validation summary report signed before production use). For SaaS, obtain vendor validation packages per release and perform customer-side risk-based verification of configured workflows before the new version is used for GMP batches; the system should support staged release (validation tenant before production tenant) and record the version in force for each batch.
verification_test: Confirm each production release has an approved validation summary before its first GMP use; confirm each batch record shows the software and configuration version under which it was executed.

document: EU GMP Annex 15 Qualification and Validation
version_or_date: Published 30 March 2015; in operation since 1 October 2015
status: final (current); no revision in progress found
notes: Official PDF (expected location): https://health.ec.europa.eu/system/files/2016-11/2015-10_annex15_0.pdf . IMPORTANT: the web-search budget for this session ran out before Annex 15 clause wording could be cross-checked, so all A15 lines below rest on prior knowledge of the text and are marked verified=false; clause numbers are best recollection and should be confirmed against the PDF.

requirement: Process validation has to show that the quality attributes and process parameters judged important for a validated state and acceptable quality are met consistently; critical parameters and attributes, and their ranges, come out of development/validation knowledge and govern routine manufacture.
system_implications: The master batch record must hold CPPs and quality-relevant in-process controls as structured, typed fields with units, precision and the validated ranges (e.g., normal operating range vs proven acceptable range), each tagged with its source (validation report / MA). Tablets: granulation endpoint, drying LOD, blend time, compression force, tablet weight/hardness/thickness, coating parameters. Injectables: compounding and bioburden hold times, filtration pressure/time, filter integrity results, fill weight/volume, stopper/crimp parameters, sterilisation F0/time-temperature. Values outside validated ranges must be blocked or force a deviation.
verification_test: For each CPP in a sample recipe confirm range, unit and source reference are configured; enter a value outside the validated range and confirm the configured blocking/deviation behaviour.

requirement: Manufacturers must keep monitoring product quality over the lifecycle to show the process stays in a state of control, evaluating relevant trends; ongoing verification runs under an approved protocol or equivalent with a written report, uses statistical tools where suitable to judge variability and capability, feeds the product quality review, looks at gradual changes over time, and has its scope and frequency revisited periodically.
system_implications: The eBMR is a primary data source for OPV: store every CPP/IPC result as structured data linked to batch, equipment, material lots and recipe version; provide a validated, audit-trailed export or API to SPC tools (or built-in control charts and capability indices); allow enhanced sampling plans to be switched on by approved change; guarantee the exported data equals the batch record (checksums, record counts).
verification_test: Export CPP data for N batches, recompute from the source records and confirm exact match; confirm control-chart limits and sampling plans are version-controlled configuration; confirm a trend-rule breach can be flagged for review.

clause: 5 (Continuous and hybrid process verification; concurrent validation)
requirement: Continuous process verification (e.g., with in-line/at-line PAT and multivariate monitoring) may replace or complement traditional validation. Concurrent validation is only for exceptional, justified cases, and its results and conclusions must be documented and made available to the QP before the batch is certified.
system_implications: Link PAT/historian time-series (e.g., NIR blend monitoring for tablets; in-line particle or weight monitoring) to the batch with synchronised timestamps and model version. Mark batches made under concurrent validation or under a validation protocol with a visible status that the QP cockpit shows together with the protocol/report status; block certification until the relevant validation results are approved.
verification_test: Flag a test batch as concurrent-validation; confirm the QP cockpit shows it and certification is blocked until the linked validation result is approved; confirm PAT data are linked with matching timestamps.

requirement: Changes that could affect product quality or the validated state (processes, equipment, materials, systems) must go through documented change control within the PQS with impact assessment, and equipment, facilities, utilities and systems must be re-evaluated at suitable intervals to confirm they remain in a state of control.
system_implications: Master record/recipe changes must reference an approved change control and its validation impact assessment before becoming effective. At execution, the eBMR should check the qualification, calibration and maintenance status of each piece of equipment, room and utility scanned into a step, and block use (or force a deviation) when status is expired or out of tolerance. Injectables: include sterilisers, depyrogenation tunnels, isolators/RABS, filling machines and integrity testers.
verification_test: Attempt to make a recipe effective without a change-control reference (blocked); scan equipment with expired calibration into a step (blocked or deviation raised); confirm the status check is logged in the batch record.

requirement: Cleaning validation must take into account how long equipment may wait between use and cleaning and between cleaning and next use, which sets validated dirty-hold and clean-hold times.
system_implications: Equipment status in the eBMR/electronic logbook must carry timestamps for end-of-use, cleaning completion and the resulting expiry of the clean status; line clearance and equipment-selection steps must reject equipment whose clean-hold has expired or whose dirty-hold was exceeded before cleaning (forcing re-cleaning or a deviation). Previous product and cleaning method used must be visible to the operator and reviewer.
verification_test: Set a short clean-hold limit in a test configuration, let it expire and attempt to use the equipment (blocked/deviation); confirm the check and timestamps appear in the batch record.

meaning: It must be possible to tell who (person) or what (system/instrument) created or changed each piece of data and when; in an eBMR this means authenticated user identity, device ID and timestamp stored with every value and change.
source: EU GMP Chapter 4 draft revision (July 2025), ALCOA++ definitions (definition content confirmed via secondary excerpt). The same term is listed as part of ALCOA in FDA Guidance 'Data Integrity and Compliance With Drug CGMP: Q&A' (Dec 2018) and in the EMA GMP data integrity Q&A (Aug 2016).

meaning: Data must stay readable and understandable for as long as they are kept, and corrections must not hide the original entry; electronically this means human-readable rendering (not only codes) and visible change history.
source: EU GMP Chapter 4 draft revision (July 2025), ALCOA++ definitions (content confirmed via secondary excerpt); also listed in FDA DI Q&A (Dec 2018) ALCOA.

meaning: Data must be recorded when the activity or observation happens, not reconstructed later; an eBMR should time-stamp with a trusted clock at the moment of entry and flag late entries.
source: EU GMP Chapter 4 draft revision (July 2025), ALCOA++ definitions (content confirmed via secondary excerpt); FDA DI Q&A (Dec 2018) uses the wording 'contemporaneously recorded'. Also consistent with current EU GMP Chapter 4 expectation that records are made when each action is taken.

meaning: The first capture of the data (the source record, including its dynamic electronic form and metadata) must be kept, or a verified true/certified copy that preserves full content and meaning; a PDF print of an electronic record is not automatically the original.
source: EU GMP Chapter 4 draft revision (July 2025), ALCOA++ definitions (content confirmed via secondary excerpt); FDA DI Q&A (Dec 2018) phrases it as 'original or a true copy'.

meaning: Data must correctly reflect what actually happened or was measured - free of errors, with edits only through documented, justified and traceable corrections; supported by validated calculations, calibrated instruments and verification of critical manual entries.
source: EU GMP Chapter 4 draft revision (July 2025) ALCOA++ list (exact definition wording not verified in this session); listed as ALCOA in FDA DI Q&A (Dec 2018).

meaning: All data needed to reconstruct the activity must be present - every result including repeats, failures and invalidated values, plus the metadata and audit trail; nothing may be silently omitted or deleted.
source: EU GMP Chapter 4 draft revision (July 2025) ALCOA++ list (definition wording not verified in this session). Also defined in EMA 'Guideline on computerised systems and electronic data in clinical trials' (EMA/INS/GCP/112288/2023) - a GCP document, cited only as supporting EU usage. FDA DI Q&A (Dec 2018) names completeness as part of its data integrity definition.

meaning: Data should be recorded in a uniform, expected way and in logical sequence (e.g., date/time stamps in order, same units and formats), so that contradictions or out-of-sequence entries stand out.
source: EU GMP Chapter 4 draft revision (July 2025) ALCOA++ list (definition wording not verified in this session); supporting EU usage in EMA GCP computerised systems guideline (2023). FDA DI Q&A (Dec 2018) names consistency as part of its data integrity definition.

meaning: Records must be stored on durable, protected media/formats so they survive intact and usable for the whole retention period (backups, archives, format migration without loss).
source: EU GMP Chapter 4 draft revision (July 2025) ALCOA++ list (definition wording not verified in this session); supporting EU usage in EMA GCP computerised systems guideline (2023).

meaning: Data must be retrievable in readable form whenever needed - for review, batch certification, audits and inspections - throughout the retention period.
source: EU GMP Chapter 4 draft revision (July 2025) ALCOA++ list (definition wording not verified in this session); supporting EU usage in EMA GCP computerised systems guideline (2023), which phrases it as available when needed.

meaning: The history of the data - how it was created, changed, moved or where it is stored - must be reconstructable from recorded identifiers and audit trail entries across the whole lifecycle.
source: EU GMP Chapter 4 draft revision (July 2025), which adds Traceable to ALCOA+ to form ALCOA++ (content confirmed via secondary excerpt). Not part of the FDA 2018 ALCOA list.
EU GMP Chapter 4 Documentation (2011, in force)
requirement: Records are to be made or completed as each action is performed, and any alteration to an entry must be signed and dated, must leave the original information readable, and where appropriate must state why it was changed.
system_implications: Entry screens must record the actual execution time automatically; entries made materially later than the step (configurable threshold) are flagged as late with a mandatory justification. Corrections never overwrite: the prior value stays visible in history and on the review/print rendering, and the correction carries user e-signature, timestamp and reason. No 'edit in place' for executed steps without this correction workflow.
verification_test: Complete a step, then correct a value: confirm prior value remains visible on screen/PDF with correction signature, time and reason; back-date attempt through UI/API is impossible; late entry beyond threshold forces justification.

clause: 3.3, 4.2, 4.5, 4.6 (supplier documentation; validation records; supplier QMS; bespoke systems)
requirement: Documentation shipped with commercial off-the-shelf products must be reviewed by the regulated user to check it meets user requirements; validation documentation should include change-control records and reports on deviations found during validation; the regulated user must take reasonable steps to ensure the system was developed under an appropriate quality management system and assess the supplier accordingly; for bespoke or customised systems there should be a process for formal assessment and reporting of quality and performance measures across all lifecycle stages.
system_implications: eBMR vendors should provide a validation package (requirements, design/configuration specs, test evidence, release notes, known-issues list) and evidence of their development QMS (SDLC, code review, testing, defect management). Customer-specific extensions (custom scripts, reports, interfaces) must be treated as bespoke and carry their own lifecycle quality metrics and test evidence. Validation deviations must be recorded and resolved before release.
verification_test: Review the vendor package and audit report for SDLC evidence; confirm custom extensions have their own specifications and test results; confirm validation deviations are logged and closed or justified in the validation summary.

text: Finalisation status: the revised Annex 11, revised Chapter 4 and new Annex 22 were still drafts in the latest evidence found (secondary reports dated July-August 2026). Re-check EudraLex Volume 4 before design freeze and before go-live; the operative date and any transition period are not yet known.

Source access: health.ec.europa.eu, ema.europa.eu, gov.uk and picscheme.org were blocked by this environment's egress proxy, and the session's web-search budget was then used up. EU text was checked through web-search excerpts (verified=true means a search excerpt corroborated the point); lines marked verified=false (Annex 15, Chapter 4 clauses 4.8/4.9, Annex 11 clauses 3.3/4.2/4.5/4.6, draft Annex 11 periodic-review contents) rest on prior knowledge and need confirming against the official PDFs.

Draft Annex 11 detail wording is known only from secondary analyses. Confirm in the consultation PDF and later the final text: (a) whether audit trails must log data creation as well as change/deletion; (b) whether an administrator independent of GMP work may ever deactivate or edit an audit trail (a draft 12.3 is reported to require activation at installation, while commentators asked to remove any remaining admin option); (c) the exact e-signature rules (re-authentication, time zone, invalidation on change, trust-service/eIDAS use); (d) whether MFA is required only for remote access; (e) the section 14 periodic-review topics.

QP batch release clause: analyses report the draft drops the stand-alone Annex 11 rule that only QPs may certify via e-signature (leaving it to Annex 16) and adds QP access to audit trails. Confirm in the final text; until then keep the 2011 clause 15 control (A11-17).

Audit-trail review frequency: some vendor blogs attribute fixed monthly/quarterly review intervals to the 2025 draft. No primary evidence was found; the more consistent reading is risk-based frequency plus completion before batch release unless justified. Do not hard-code fixed intervals as a regulatory requirement; make them configurable.

Injectables edition: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022 revision) drives sterile-specific batch-record and release content (environmental monitoring, aseptic process simulation status, sterilisation and filter-integrity records, contamination control strategy). It was outside this narrow topic and should be researched separately to complete the INJECTABLES edition requirements.

Annex 22 scope may widen: after the July 2026 EMA workshop the drafting group is reported to be considering whether generative/probabilistic models could be allowed under safeguards. Product decisions on AI assistants in the eBMR should wait for the final text.

ALCOA++ definitions: the draft Chapter 4 is reported to define all ten attributes; exact definition wording for Accurate, Complete, Consistent, Enduring and Available could not be verified here. The EMA clinical-trials computerised systems guideline (2023) also defines ALCOA++ but is a GCP document; the FDA DI Q&A (Dec 2018) lists only the five core ALCOA terms and names completeness/consistency/accuracy in its definition of data integrity.
